draft.title: Conservation of energy
card: Energy cannot be made or destroyed. It can only be transferred from one object to another, or transformed from one type to another.
energy moves from one place or object to another, such as heat moving from a hot drink into a cold cup.
energy changes type, such as chemical energy in a battery becoming electrical energy and then light and heat.

In any system, the energy out equals the energy in. Useful energy plus wasted energy equals the energy put in. Wasted energy is often heat or sound that spreads into the surroundings, so it is hard to collect, but it has not disappeared.
draft.remember: Useful energy plus wasted energy always equals the energy put in. Nothing is lost or created.

a.q: A skateboard rolls across rough concrete and slows to a stop. Where does its kinetic energy go?
opts: It becomes heat and sound in the ground and air
It is destroyed because the skateboard has stopped
It stays in the skateboard as kinetic energy
It becomes new energy that adds to the total
a.why: Energy is not destroyed. The kinetic energy is transformed into wasted heat and sound, which spread into the ground and air. Saying it is destroyed is tempting because the skateboard stops, but the energy has only changed form.
a.clue: Where does the energy go if it cannot disappear?

b.q: Priya's torch battery supplies 100 J of chemical energy. The torch gives out 20 J of useful light. How much wasted energy is there, and what is it?
opts: 80 J, mostly heat in the torch and its surroundings
0 J, because the battery energy was used up
80 J, which is destroyed inside the torch
20 J, because light and heat share the energy equally
b.why: Useful energy plus wasted energy equals the 100 J put in, so 100 J minus 20 J leaves 80 J of wasted energy. It is mostly heat that spreads into the torch and the air. Calling it used up or destroyed is tempting, but energy is never destroyed.
b.clue: Useful plus wasted must equal the energy put in.

a.best: It becomes heat and sound in the ground and air

b.best: 80 J, mostly heat in the torch and its surroundings
